overview.title: What is the Philippines
paragraphs: The Philippines is a sovereign archipelagic country in Southeast Asia. Its 7,641 islands are grouped geographically into Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. Manila is the capital, and the National Capital Region is the country's center of government.

The Philippine Statistics Authority counted 112,729,484 people in the 2024 Census of Population. The count covers the country's 18 administrative regions and includes Filipinos in Philippine embassies, consulates, and missions abroad.

The Philippines proclaimed independence from Spain on 12 June 1898. The United States recognized Philippine independence on 4 July 1946. Republic Act No. 4166 later designated 12 June as Philippine Independence Day.

The 1987 Constitution defines the Philippines as a democratic and republican State. It establishes Filipino as the national language and names Filipino and English as the official languages for communication and instruction.

symbols.title: National symbols
symbols.meta: Established by Republic Act 8491 & Presidential Proclamations

flag.label: Flag
flag.title: Pambansang Watawat
flag.desc: The national flag has blue, white, and red fields, a golden-yellow sun with eight rays, and three five-pointed stars. Its design and proper use are set by Republic Act No. 8491.
flag.imageAlt: The national flag of the Philippines

anthem.label: National anthem
anthem.title: Lupang Hinirang
anthem.desc: Julián Felipe composed the music in 1898. The Filipino lyrics are based on José Palma's Spanish poem “Filipinas,” and Republic Act No. 8491 prescribes the anthem's official form.
anthem.imageAlt: Vocal sheet music for the Philippine national anthem, Lupang Hinirang

seal.label: Coat of arms
seal.title: Coat of arms of the Philippines
seal.desc: Republic Act No. 8491 prescribes the coat of arms and the Great Seal. The Great Seal is used on commissions signed by the President and on other official documents when required.
seal.imageAlt: The coat of arms of the Republic of the Philippines

bird.label: National bird
bird.title: Pithecophaga jefferyi
bird.desc: Proclamation No. 615 declared the endemic Philippine eagle the national bird in 1995 and directed government agencies to support its conservation and protection.
bird.imageAlt: A Philippine eagle perched against a soft green background

tree.label: National tree
tree.title: Pterocarpus indicus
tree.desc: Proclamation No. 652 declared the narra the national tree in 1934. It is a native hardwood species found in the Philippines and elsewhere in Southeast Asia.
tree.imageAlt: The leafy canopy and trunk of a mature narra tree

flower.label: National flower
flower.title: Jasminum sambac
flower.desc: Proclamation No. 652 declared the sampaguita the national flower in 1934. The small white jasmine is widely cultivated for its fragrant blossoms.
flower.imageAlt: White sampaguita flowers among glossy green leaves

scholarNote.title: Reading the historical record
scholarNote.body: Dates for prehistoric finds are approximate. Written accounts, objects and oral traditions offer different kinds of evidence, and interpretations can change as research develops.

entries.title: Early human activity
entries.body: Stone tools and rhinoceros bones bearing cut marks, excavated in Kalinga, provide evidence of early hominin activity in Luzon. The species responsible has not been identified.

entries.yr: Tens of thousands of years ago
entries.title: The Tabon Cave discoveries
entries.body: Excavations at the Tabon Cave Complex in Palawan uncovered early Homo sapiens remains and evidence of toolmaking and burial practices. Finds from different periods help researchers study the long human history of the islands.

entries.title: Laguna Copperplate Inscription
entries.body: This copperplate records the settlement of a debt. Its language and script show connections between communities in the archipelago and the wider trading world of Southeast Asia.

entries.title: Islam and the southern sultanates
entries.body: Islam spread through trade and religious networks in the southern islands. Muslim communities and, later, sultanates became important centers of political, commercial and religious life.

entries.title: Magellan’s expedition and Mactan
entries.body: The expedition led by Ferdinand Magellan reached the archipelago while sailing for Spain. Magellan died at Mactan in a battle with forces led by Lapulapu. Permanent Spanish settlement began decades later.

entries.title: Spanish settlement and administration
entries.body: Miguel López de Legazpi established a Spanish settlement in Cebu in 1565. Manila became the colonial capital in 1571. Spanish administration expanded unevenly across the islands, alongside communities that maintained their independence.

entries.title: Philippine Revolution
entries.body: The Katipunan, founded in 1892 with Andrés Bonifacio among its organizers, began an armed revolution against Spanish colonial rule. The conflict led to revolutionary governments and the declaration of independence in 1898.

entries.title: Declaration of independence
entries.body: Philippine independence was proclaimed at Emilio Aguinaldo’s home in Kawit, Cavite. The Philippine flag was displayed and Julián Felipe’s march, which became the national anthem, was performed.

entries.title: Treaty of Paris and the Philippine-American War
entries.body: Under the Treaty of Paris, Spain ceded the Philippines to the United States. Filipino forces contested American sovereignty, and war began in 1899. Although the United States declared the war ended in 1902, armed resistance continued in some areas.

entries.title: Commonwealth inaugurated
entries.body: Following the 1934 Tydings–McDuffie Act, the Commonwealth was inaugurated as a transitional government toward independence. Manuel L. Quezon served as its first president.

entries.title: War and Japanese occupation
entries.body: Japan invaded in December 1941. The occupation brought widespread loss of life and destruction, including the Bataan Death March and the Battle of Manila. Filipino guerrillas and Allied forces fought in the campaign to end the occupation.

entries.title: Independence recognized
entries.body: The United States recognized Philippine independence, and Manuel Roxas became president of the Third Republic. The annual Independence Day observance later shifted to June 12 to commemorate the 1898 declaration.

entries.title: Declaration of martial law
entries.body: President Ferdinand E. Marcos placed the Philippines under martial law through Proclamation No. 1081, dated 21 September 1972, citing rebellion and threats to public order. The period brought expanded presidential powers, restrictions on the press and civil liberties, and documented human rights violations. Martial law was formally lifted on 17 January 1981 through Proclamation No. 2045; Marcos remained president until February 1986.

entries.title: EDSA People Power Revolution
entries.body: Large civilian demonstrations, following a disputed presidential election and the withdrawal of support by key military officials, led to a change in government. Corazon C. Aquino took office on February 25, and Ferdinand E. Marcos left the country.

entries.title: The 1987 Constitution
entries.body: Ratified in a national plebiscite, the Constitution established the framework for the present presidential system. It provides for a Bill of Rights, three branches of government, constitutional commissions and limits on the exercise of public power.

entries.title: Local Government Code
entries.body: Republic Act No. 7160 transferred specified functions, responsibilities and resources to local governments. It remains a central framework for how provinces, cities, municipalities and barangays deliver public services.

entries.title: Establishment of BARMM
entries.body: Following plebiscites on the Bangsamoro Organic Law, the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao replaced the ARMM. The law provides for a parliamentary regional government within the Philippine constitutional system.

overview.title: Historical Overview
paragraphs: The Philippines' history spans thousands of years, beginning with the migration of Austronesian peoples. These early settlers developed sophisticated societies, trading with various Asian civilizations and developing unique cultural traditions.

The arrival of Ferdinand Magellan in 1521 marked the beginning of Spanish colonization, which would last for over three centuries. This period saw the widespread adoption of Christianity and the establishment of colonial institutions that would significantly influence Filipino society.

Following the Spanish-American War, the Philippines came under American rule, leading to significant changes in education, governance, and society. The country achieved independence in 1946 and has since worked to build a modern nation while preserving its rich cultural heritage.

intro.title: Many communities. An interconnected history.
intro.body: The history of the Philippines reaches far beyond the founding of the republic. Archaeology, written records and community traditions reveal different experiences across the archipelago. This timeline introduces selected events and links to records for further reading.

milestones.title: Declaration and recognition of independence
milestones.declaration: On 12 June 1898, independence was proclaimed in Kawit, Cavite. June 12 is observed as Philippine Independence Day.
milestones.recognition: On 4 July 1946, the United States formally recognized the independence of the Republic of the Philippines.

regionalOverview.title: Regional Overview
paragraphs: The Philippines is divided into three main geographical divisions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. These are further subdivided into 18 regions, each with its own administrative center, cultural identity, and economic focus.

Each region showcases unique traditions, dialects, and cuisines, contributing to the country's rich cultural tapestry. From the mountain tribes of the Cordilleras to the seafaring communities of the Visayas, the diversity of Filipino regional cultures is remarkable.

The regions also vary in their economic activities, from the industrial and service-oriented National Capital Region to the agricultural heartlands of Central Luzon and the resource-rich provinces of Mindanao.
